## `robotstxt` example: MU bulletin

In the chunk below we used the `robotstxt` package to check if we are allowed to write a program that scrapes the page <https://bulletin.miamioh.edu/courses-instruction/isa/>.

```{r bulletin}
robotstxt::paths_allowed(
  paths = "courses-instruction/isa/",
  domain = "https://bulletin.miamioh.edu/"
)
```
The `TRUE` above means that we are allowed to scrape it.

## `robotstxt`: Wikipedia
```{r}
robotstxt::paths_allowed(
  paths = "wiki/Miami_RedHawks_football",
  domain = "en.wikipedia.org",
  bot = "*"
)

```

## `robotstxt`: Linkedin
```{r linkedin}
# In some cases, the robotstxt provides inconsistent answers
# typically, you get a warning with the answer that is incorrect
# solution: drop the trailing slash from the URL
# even better, check with the robots.txt (which is the groun truth)
robotstxt::paths_allowed(
  paths = "/jobs/",
  domain = "https://www.linkedin.com",
  bot = "*"
)

```

## `robotstxt`: Indeed
```{r indeed}

robotstxt::paths_allowed(
  paths = "/jobs and /viewjob",
  domain = "www.indeed.com",
  bot = "*"
)
```

## Scrape Miami's Bulletin for ISA
```{r scrape}
# checking whether we are allowed to scrape this info
# This was done above and found to be TRUE

# I will load the backend of the HTML into R using 
# [a] rvest::read_html() | sometimes rvest::read_html_live if he page has some dynamic content
# [b] in some cases, we will craft this as a request as shown in slides httr2::request() > .... > httr2:resp_body_html()
isa_courses_in_r = rvest::read_html("https://bulletin.miamioh.edu/courses-instruction/isa/")

# we will extract the course titles, which we can do in a single pipeline
# given that they look the same on the rendered web page in Chrome
# (bolded, same font size, same font type)

# CSS selector was obtained by:
# [a] highlighting what we wanted to pull (ISA 401 course title) in Chrome -> right click
# inspect -> right click -> copy -> copy selector
# [b] from this specifc example, we were able to get just the title for ISA 401
# because we had `:nth-child(24)` -> if you were to drop it --> you get all the course titles
isa_courses_in_r |> 
  rvest::html_elements("#sc_sccoursedescs > div > p.courseblocktitle > strong") |> 
  rvest::html_text2() -> isa_titles

# course descriptions [using selector gadget, which does not always work]
# but when it works it is easier

isa_courses_in_r |> 
  rvest::html_elements(".courseblockdesc") |> 
  rvest::html_text2() -> isa_desc

df = data.frame(title = isa_titles, descrpition = isa_desc)

```
